paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates cosine similarity values as a function of subset size \(|S|\) for two methods (“Weight averaging” and “QLoRA”). The x-axis is labeled \(|S|\), uses a linear scale, and spans integer values from 2 to 10, with major tick labels shown at 2-unit intervals (2, 4, 6, 8, 10). The y-axis is labeled “Cosine similarity.”, uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0.1 up to about 0.35, with major tick labels at 0.1 increments (0.1, 0.2, 0.3). The “Weight averaging” series is drawn as a blue dashed line with filled square markers, decreasing from about 0.33 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.23 at \(|S|=10\), with intermediate points around 0.28 (\(|S|=3\)), 0.25 (\(|S|=4\)), ~0.245 (\(|S|=5\)), and then gradually flattening near ~0.24–0.23 from \(|S|=6\) through 10. The “QLoRA” series is drawn as a green dashed line with filled circular markers, decreasing from about 0.29 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.165 at \(|S|=10\), passing through roughly 0.26 (\(|S|=3\)), ~0.21 (\(|S|=4\)), ~0.20 (\(|S|=5\)), ~0.185 (\(|S|=6\)), and then continuing downward more gradually around ~0.175 (\(|S|=7\)) to ~0.17 (\(|S|=8\)) and slightly below ~0.17 by \(|S|=9\)–10.
